subject: Recap & next steps: Novaterra leadership alignment and pilot path
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Yu <samantha.yu@novaterra.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@novaterra.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps: Novaterra leadership alignment and pilot path

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call with your leadership team and suggested next steps so we have alignment going into procurement: 

Key pain points you confirmed
- Intermittent p95 latency spikes on peak batch inference (current infra peaks ~2.2s).
- Unpredictable token spend from bursty user patterns — finance needs a cleaner forecast.
- Model version drift and rollback complexity when pushing updates.
- Data residency / keys: legal requires clear KMS controls and audit logs for PII.

Stated business goals
- Reduce p95 latency by ~40% on average for core user flows (target ~1.2s).
- Cap monthly inference cost growth to <=10% QoQ while scaling usage.
- Pilot must demonstrate repeatable rollout + auditability for a single regulated EU region.

Proposed procurement path (your ask + our recommendation)
1) 6-week pilot (scope: 3 models, production-ish load, observability + cost breakdown).
2) Security questionnaire + SOC2 snapshot exchange in parallel (we can send SOC2 Type II report + short Q&A).
3) Pilot acceptance -> SOW for dedicated capacity and rollout timeline -> PO.

Asks / deliverables from Redwood by EOD Monday (Mar 5)
- Draft pilot SOW (attached: pilot-sow-draft.docx).
- Compact benchmark summary for the model classes we discussed (attached CSV).
- Initial security answers for your legal (we'll follow-up with the full security pack).

Open questions for Novaterra
- Who is the procurement contact (name + email + PO cadence)?
- Is Rajiv (CTO) expected to sign off on pilot results or only the full contract?
- Any strict blackout dates for pilot traffic in late March?

I'll coordinate with Jordan and Dylan on technical prep and the security deliverables. If this captures everything, we'll kick the SOW and security notes over Monday.

Best,
Tessa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pilot-sow-draft.docx]
[Attachment: redwood-benchmarks-compact-20280302.csv]
From: Samantha Yu <samantha.yu@novaterra.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@novaterra.com>, Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@novaterra.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 18:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: Novaterra leadership alignment and pilot path

Tessa —

Appreciate the clear summary. This matches how the executive team heard it. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement contact: we use centralized procurement — please route SOW/PO communications to procurement@novaterra.com and loop in Tom (he's handling the initial legal review).
- Decision flow: Rajiv (CTO) wants to see the pilot telemetry and a short 30-min readout; final approval goes via Finance for the annual commit after pilot acceptance.
- Timeline: 6-week pilot sounds right. Ideally pilot start mid-March; we have a product freeze the week of Mar 20 so prefer start Mar 13–19.

We'll also send you the security questionnaire template Tom's team uses. Can your SOC2 snapshot and answers arrive by Monday as you suggested? That will unblock legal.

I'll have procurement reach out with PO cadence after they see the SOW.

Thanks — Samantha
VP, Growth & Product Operations
Novaterra
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Yu <samantha.yu@novaterra.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: Novaterra leadership alignment and pilot path

Thanks Samantha —

Quick technical notes / clarifications so the pilot SOW is precise: 
- Pilot scope: we'll include two production-like traffic profiles (interactive chat and asynchronous batch scoring) to capture both tail latency and cost characteristics.
- For model versioning, we'll demo Canary rollouts with automatic rollback on perf regressions — will include the rollback window and metrics in the SOW.
- Data residency: for EU-region testing we propose a VPC private deployment variant (no data egress) — requires KMS key exchange and an SBO for audit access.

Tessa / Dylan — can you confirm who will own the KMS key exchange operationally on Redwood's side so we can note it in the SOW?

Jordan
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Yu <samantha.yu@novaterra.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: Novaterra leadership alignment and pilot path

[Attachment: security-answers-novaterra.pdf]

- Dylan: security checklist + KMS contact (deliverable: Mon EOD)

- Tessa: finalize SOW narrative and send to procurement@novaterra.com (deliverable: Mon EOD)

I'll flag any blocker to Tessa immediately.

Dylan Brooks
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@novaterra.com>

Cc: Rajiv Patel <rajiv.patel@novaterra.com>, procurement@novaterra.com
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps: Novaterra leadership alignment and pilot path

Tessa / team —

Received the SOW and security stubs you uploaded this morning; procurement is ready to accept a pilot PO for a limited-scope engagement. From legal's side the key items we'll verify during the pilot are: audit log access, KMS controls, and clear acceptance criteria for the telemetry readout.

We're good to start target week of Mar 13. Please send the PO instructions to procurement@novaterra.com and copy me. Rajiv will join the pilot readout once the telemetry shows stability.

Thanks — Tom
Director, Procurement & Vendor Risk
Novaterra
